item.title: Commands
item.description:
wctr

The client. It finds the daemon at -H unix:///path, else $WCTR_HOST, else unix:///var/run/wctr.sock.

Command Flags
pull IMAGE IMAGE is a registry reference or oci:<dir>[:<ref.name>]
images -q
run IMAGE [COMMAND] [ARG...] --rm, -d/--detach, --name, -e/--env KEY=value (or KEY from the shell), --entrypoint, -w/--workdir, -m/--memory, -v NAME:/path[:ro] (v0.8.0), --network NAME (v0.10.0), --network-alias NAME (v0.14.0), --gpu (v0.13.0), -p/--publish [ip:][hostPort:]containerPort[/tcp|udp] (the ip defaults to 127.0.0.1), -P/--publish-all, --expose PORT[/proto] (v0.22.0), --restart no|always|unless-stopped|on-failure[:N] (v0.25.0; not with --rm; see Restart policies)
port CONTAINER [PRIVATE_PORT[/PROTO]] where a running container’s ports are published, e.g. 80/tcp -> 127.0.0.1:8080 (v0.22.0)
ps -a/--all, -q; a PORTS column as Docker writes it (v0.22.0)
logs CONTAINER -f/--follow
rm CONTAINER... -f/--force
rmi IMAGE... -f/--force
commit CONTAINER [REPO[:TAG]] -m/--message, -a/--author, -c/--change (CMD, ENTRYPOINT, ENV, EXPOSE, LABEL, ONBUILD, STOPSIGNAL, USER, VOLUME, WORKDIR): the container’s changes as one OCI layer on the parent’s, with a history entry; without a name, a <none> image addressable by ID (v0.12.0)
tag SOURCE TARGET another name for an image; a tag that moves leaves the old image as <none> (v0.12.0)
inspect NAME|ID... containers, then images
build, compose wctr build and wctr compose, built into wctr since cmd/wctr v0.1.0; they use wctr’s -H, which goes before the subcommand
exec [-d] [-i] [-t] [-e K=V] [-w DIR] CONTAINER CMD... a further process in a running container, in its process group; needs --wasi engine; exits with the command’s status; -t gives it a terminal (the engine does the line editing and echo); -u accepts only root or 0 (engine v0.20.0). In the browser executor since v0.26.0: the process runs in its own worker inside the container’s process group, counts against its limits and is killed with it. -t follows window resizes since v0.27.0: SIGWINCH on unix, a 2 Hz size sampling on Windows, wasip1 and js
kill CONTAINER...
start CONTAINER... -a/--all (v0.5.0)
stop CONTAINER... -t, accepted and ignored (v0.5.0)
restart CONTAINER... -t, accepted and ignored (v0.5.0)
diff CONTAINER (v0.4.0)
events --since, --until, filters on type, event, container, image, volume and label (v0.6.0)
stats (v0.7.0)
volume create|ls|inspect|rm|prune (v0.8.0)
network create|ls|inspect|rm (v0.10.0)
network connect [--alias NAME] NETWORK CONTAINER a running container at once (v0.14.0)
network disconnect [-f] NETWORK CONTAINER (v0.14.0)
network prune [-f] [--filter label=K[=V]] unused networks (v0.14.0)
system df -v (v0.4.0)
system prune -a, -f (v0.4.0)
version
completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell prints the completion script for that shell (v0.3.0)

wctr run pulls an image it does not have.

A WebAssembly guest has no signals, so wctr stop kills the container at once: -t is accepted for compatibility and ignored. In the API, /attach is a plain streamed response, not a hijacked connection.

For builders (v0.12.0, API only for now)

  • POST /images/load takes an OCI image layout as a tar; each index.json entry is named by io.containerd.image.name or org.opencontainers.image.ref.name, else <none>. It is checked as a pull is, and nothing is read from the host.
  • PUT /containers/{id}/archive?path=DIR extracts a tar into a container (relative clean names only, no devices, paths resolved inside the container, its quota applies), and GET returns a tar of a path. These two routes accept uploads up to 1 GiB by default; every other request is limited to 1 MiB.
  • GET /images/{name}/json shows the full image config, the history, and RootFS.Layers as diff_ids. Dangling images appear as <none>.
  • HEAD on the archive route returns only the path’s stat, without building a tar (v0.14.0).
  • The Go client filters lists through ContainersFiltered, NetworksFiltered and VolumesFiltered, which take an api.Filters. v0.18.0 had changed the signatures of Containers, Networks and Volumes to take filters, which broke the dashboard; v0.21.0 restored them, and a new CI job compiles downstream modules against the engine.
  • A start refused before the process exists (a port, a network, a volume) is recorded as an exit with code 128 and the reason, as Docker records it: a run --rm returns at once and its container is removed (v0.22.0). Since v0.23.0, wctr run exits 125 when the daemon refuses the start.
  • Other modules add commands to wctr through an extension hook, cli.Options.Extra; wctr build and wctr compose use it. wctr build needs a wctrd of v0.12.0 or later (v0.17.0 for shell-form RUN).

Events (v0.6.0)

wctr events and GET /events stream NDJSON. --since and --until bound the range, and the filters are type, event, container, image, volume, network and label. The last 1024 events are kept, and a reader that is too slow is cut off.

Stats (v0.7.0)

wctr stats and the stats endpoint report memory against its limit, bytes written, layer and log size, and pids. CPU is not measured: a WebAssembly guest gives no CPU accounting, so it is shown as --.

Volumes (v0.8.0)

wctr volume create|ls|inspect|rm|prune, and wctr run -v NAME:/path[:ro]. Only named volumes exist: a host path is refused. A volume is shared between containers, :ro is enforced, and volumes survive a restart and a page reload. They appear in system df and in inspect.

Persistence (v0.4.0)

Containers survive a wctrd restart: they are kept under --data-root in containers/ (state, exit code, logs and written files). A container that was running comes back exited with code 137, and a --rm container is removed. An entry that is corrupted is dropped and reported.

Exit status of wctr run

The container’s own, or:

Code Meaning
125 the CLI or the daemon failed
126 not a WebAssembly module
127 module not found
134 the module trapped
137 killed, or the wall-clock timeout

Restart policies

run --restart and HostConfig.RestartPolicy (engine v0.25.0), as Docker’s:

  • always restarts a container whenever it exits, and starts it with the engine;
  • unless-stopped does the same, except that the engine leaves it stopped if a user stopped it;
  • on-failure[:N] restarts it when it exits with a code other than 0, at most N times (0: no bound);
  • no is the default.

A user’s stop or kill ends the policy until the next start, which counts from zero. Each restart waits first: 100 ms, doubled after every run shorter than 10 s, at most a minute. Meanwhile the container is restarting: ps lists it as Restarting (code) … ago, and rm needs -f. A start the engine refuses (a volume, a network, a port) is not retried. inspect shows HostConfig.RestartPolicy, RestartCount and State.Restarting. A policy cannot be combined with --rm.

Health checks

run --health-cmd CMD, --health-interval, --health-timeout, --health-start-period, --health-start-interval, --health-retries and --no-healthcheck (engine v0.28.0), as well as an image’s HEALTHCHECK and Config.Healthcheck. The test (CMD argv, CMD-SHELL through /bin/sh -c, or NONE) runs inside the running container through the exec machinery, every interval (default 30 s; 5 s during the start period), and is killed after the timeout (default 30 s, exit code −1). A pass makes the container healthy; retries consecutive failures (default 3) make it unhealthy; failures in the start period do not count. Fields left empty are taken from the image’s check. inspect shows State.Health (Status, FailingStreak, and the last 5 results with at most 4 KiB of output each), ps shows Up … (healthy), and each change of status is a health_status event (healthy or unhealthy; --filter event=health_status). Probes stop with the container and are not exec events. Unlike Docker, an interval or timeout below 100 ms is refused. A CMD-SHELL probe needs a /bin/sh in the image (the shell image has one).

For embedders. An in-process engine must register wasi.WASIX in its HostModules, as wctrd does, to run the shell image or health checks.

wctrd

Flag Meaning Default
-H, --host unix:///path the socket to serve (unix only; TCP is refused, the API has no authentication) unix:///var/run/wctr.sock
--data-root where images are kept $XDG_DATA_HOME/wasmcontainers, else ~/.local/share/wasmcontainers
--memory linear-memory limit per container 256m
--run-timeout wall-clock limit per run (0 = none) 10m
--storage-quota bytes a container may write 256m
--max-containers containers at once 256
--insecure-registry host:port allow plain HTTP to that registry (loopback registries are always plain HTTP) none

Bounds on untrusted content

What Bound
blob 512 MiB
image 1 GiB, 128 layers
unpacked layers 1 GiB, 131072 files
gzip expansion ratio 200:1
logs kept 8 MiB per container
